customer_question: We are using Google Fluoride (Android Bluetooth stack). Which version should we use to avoid Consistency Check errors during Design Number registration?
question_variants: Is Google Fluoride 1.5 safe to use for Bluetooth certification?
Why does Fluoride 1.6 fail the GAP-GATT Consistency Check?
Are there any Fluoride versions that pass the SIG inter-layer check?
actual_issue: All currently known versions of Google Fluoride (1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6) have an internal GAP-GATT ICS inconsistency. Specifically: when GATT (7/5) or (7/6) is Supported, the rules require at least one of GAP (25/5 or 35/5) / GAP (25/6 or 35/6) respectively to also be Supported, and this is not satisfied — and similarly, GATT (1/2 and 4/15), (1/2 and 4/16), and (1/2 and 4/22) being Supported each require GATT (4/25) to be Mandatory, which is also not satisfied. The Consistency Check flags these as fatal Invalid findings, which blocks Design Number registration. There is no known fixed version of Fluoride as of this thread. The only alternatives are to switch to BlueZ or another already-registered Host Stack, or wait for Fluoride to release a corrected version.
plain_english_explanation: Google Fluoride's ICS has a built-in conflict between its GAP and GATT declarations: certain GATT features it claims to support require corresponding GAP features to also be marked supported, and Fluoride's ICS does not mark them, so the Consistency Check flags it as fatal Invalid. This affects all tested Fluoride versions (1.3 through 1.6) identically. Customers using Fluoride cannot obtain a Design Number until either Fluoride is fixed or they switch to a compliant Host Stack such as BlueZ.
consultant_answer: All Fluoride versions 1.3-1.6 tested produced the same fatal GAP-GATT ICS inconsistency (GATT 7/5 and 7/6 requiring GAP 25/5,35/5 or 25/6,35/6; and GATT 1/2+4/15, 1/2+4/16, 1/2+4/22 requiring GATT 4/25) and ALL will block Design Number registration. The module/Controller QDID is irrelevant since GAP and GATT are Host Subsystem layers. Recommend switching to BlueZ or another already-registered, Invalid-free Host Stack. The consultant speculated that Bluetooth SIG added this GAP/GATT ICS check rule after these Fluoride versions were originally registered, which is why it was not caught earlier.
decision_logic:
1. Identify the Host Stack as Google Fluoride.
2. Run Consistency Check on a trial project combining the module/Controller QDID with each Fluoride version (1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6) before adding profiles.
3. Each version produces fatal GAP-GATT Invalid findings → Consistency Check fails regardless of module/Controller used.
4. Cannot be resolved by changing module QDID or SoC, since GAP/GATT are Host-layer.
5. Must switch Host Stack to BlueZ or another compliant, already-registered option, or wait for a corrected Fluoride release.
final_recommendation: Do not proceed with Fluoride if Design Number registration is required under QPRDv3.0. Advise the customer to use BlueZ or another compliant Host Stack. Document this limitation clearly at project intake.
risk_if_done_wrong: Starting a registration project with Fluoride and discovering the GAP-GATT block mid-project wastes test and registration fees, and delays product launch until the Host Stack is changed.
